content: This product information does not guarantee that the medication is safe, effective, or suitable for you. It is not intended to replace individualized medical advice or the guidance of your healthcare professional. Always consult your healthcare provider for comprehensive information about this product and your specific health needs. This medication, commonly known by the brand name Lamisil, is used to treat various fungal skin infections, including ringworm, athlete's foot, and jock itch. It is also effective in managing a skin condition called pityriasis (tinea versicolor), a fungal infection that causes discoloration of the skin on the neck, chest, arms, or legs. How to Use: This medication is for external use on the skin only. Before application, clean and thoroughly dry the affected area. Apply a thin layer of the medication to the affected area and the surrounding skin, typically once or twice daily, as directed on the product packaging. If you have any questions, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Wash your hands after applying the medication unless the treated area includes the hands. Avoid contact with the eyes, nose, mouth, or inside the vagina. Do not use the medication more frequently or for a longer duration than prescribed. Use the medication consistently to achieve the best results. Continue using the medication for the full treatment period, even if symptoms improve after a few days. The condition may continue to improve after completing the treatment. It may take several weeks after treatment for the infection to fully heal. Side Effects: Common side effects include burning, irritation, or itching at the application site. If your doctor has prescribed this medication, they have determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this medication are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance. Precautions: Before using terbinafine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other allylamine antifungals (e.g., naftifine), or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. During pregnancy, use this medication only if clearly needed. Consult your doctor for advice. It is unknown if this drug passes into breast milk when applied to the skin. However, other forms of this medication, when taken orally, do pass into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Overdose: This medication may be harmful if swallowed. If someone has overdosed and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Additional Notes: If treating athlete's foot, wear well-fitting, ventilated shoes. When treating pityriasis, your normal skin color may not return immediately. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Storage: Store the medication at room temperature. Do not refrigerate. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in May 2024. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete and personalized advice regarding this product and your health.
